result.summary:
Independently re-ran `grep -rniE --include="*.md" "hard gate|structurally impossible|Backend gate|Frontend gate" docs/anti-patterns.md` myself. Result: exactly FIVE real line-matches -- 1578, 1611, 1689, 1910, 1920 -- matching both the prior FAIL's finding and CODE-DESIGNER's rework-2 recount exactly. The corrected bullet in docs/migration/decisions/0018-branch-protection-posture.md now reads 'docs/anti-patterns.md (five hits, across three distinct anti-pattern sections)' and itemizes each of the five lines individually.

Spot-checked the bullet's claims against the actual file content at each line:
- Line 1578: bullet quotes 'This was caught only at CI (PR #681's first `Backend gate` run failed on it)', attributed to the 'top-level `status` field' anti-pattern section. Confirmed verbatim in docs/anti-patterns.md at that line, inside that section (the PR #681/lint_handoffs status-enum incident).
- Line 1611: bullet quotes '...instead make it structurally impossible (e.g. ORCH greps every handoff...)', same section, described as a proposed future ORCH-side check. Confirmed verbatim -- this is forward-looking tooling language, not a description of existing enforcement.
- Line 1689: bullet quotes 'REQ-167's PR #688 failed CI's backend gate on the very first run', attributed to a separate 'mix format --check-formatted' section. Confirmed verbatim, and confirmed as a distinct incident (formatter line-length rejection) from line 1578's status-enum mistake -- different section header, different root cause.
- Line 1910: bullet quotes '...the same narrow ISS-0069-focused task CI's backend gate runs', attributed to the 'dead default argument' section's REQ-195 recurrence. Confirmed verbatim and confirmed as a third distinct incident (compiler warning surfacing only under a specific mix task).
- Line 1920: bullet quotes '...past FIVE separate hard gates that each ran a real `mix compile`/`mix test` pass on this exact file', attributed to the same section's later REQ-203 recurrence. Confirmed verbatim -- a different occurrence of the same dead-default-argument anti-pattern, not a restatement of 1910.

All five section attributions and all five quoted excerpts check out against the real file. The bullet's closing conclusion -- 'None of the five lines asserts a current, general claim about main's merge protection; they recount what happened in past CI/review runs or propose unrelated future tooling' -- holds on inspection for all five: 1578/1689/1910/1920 are all past-tense incident narration about CI/review gates catching mistakes, and 1611 is explicitly proposed future tooling ('instead make it structurally impossible'), not a description of anything currently enforced. No line in this set makes any claim, past or present, about git branch-protection / merge-blocking on `main` specifically -- they are all about review/CI gates catching bugs in PRs, a different mechanism from what this ADR is about. Conclusion (no correction needed to anti-patterns.md) stands.

Verified via `git diff be93708c..f56ecb1d` that the only content change is this one bullet in the Consequences section of 0018-branch-protection-posture.md (plus the two handoff JSON files' own bookkeeping fields -- handoff_id, task.description, summary, rework_count -- which is expected process metadata, not design content). Decisions (a)/(b)/(c)/(d), the Step 1-4 gh api/gh CLI command sequences, the AC3 live-verification plan, and the other eight already-passed file characterizations (AGENT_SYSTEM.md, WF-02_requirement_implementation.md, WF-01_requirement_development.md, HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, 0014-scripting-plugin-runtime-strategy.md, GIT_SETUP.md, 0011-frontend-ownership.md, 0017-task-queue-selection-model.md) are byte-for-byte untouched.
